## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Therese Altmann [13. September 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.166
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.166
- Datum: 13.9.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Rio, Sept. 13th, 41
Dearest mother, I have received your two letters of
Aug 19th (addressed to NY) and of Aug 22nd and hope to have
good news from you again soon and to hear that you can
stay on in the same house which you seem to like.
We have taken a home in Petropolis and will move up there some time next
week. It is quite small, really only a bungalow and separate servants
quarters as all the houses are arranged up there - I suppose still a remnant
from the days of slavery - but we like it. It is built halfway up a hill
and has a beautiful view on mountains from a big covered terrace where
I suppose Stefan will spend his days working. You walk up to it a number of
steps through a nice little garden which as the landlady promised will be
full of hortensias in summer. Behind the house immediately is the hill, but
a few steps further up the gardener is just preparing a small plateau and
he promised to build a little summer house as well - so I shall take this as
my residence during the day, and maybe later on, when the season begins
I shall change place with Stefan so as to hide him from unexpected visitors.
I have been very lucky in so far as the landlady has solved the servants'
question for me. The gardener and his wife will continue to live in the servants
quarters and he will look after the garden, act as handy-man and do errands
if necessary. He works in a factory and does all for us after his work, and
besides their living in my place I shall have nothing to do with them -
they do their own cooking etc. During the day a cook-servant will come and
do the house-work and cooking. All our friends, meaning well
without doubt, have been warning me how difficult it is with servants in
Petropolis. Those from Rio do not go up there because it is too primitive
- the cooking is done on old-fashioned stoves which have to be heated
with wood, the servants quarters are very primitive etc - and the servants
in Petropolis are supposed to be lazy and inefficient. But I am not
frightened. I know that as the gardener lives in the house I shall not be
left quite alone with all the work and I believe that after England and
USA I do not expect too much from servants. In any case we are very
glad to get settled for a few months at least and to live a quite retired
life. We both have at the moment no desire at all to see people or to go out
a lot. Even here in Rio which we both love so much, we go out very little
and are satisfied with the view from our terrace which makes up for all the
defects of the hotel which is clean and has good service but which is run too
much on the principles of the Haushaltungsschule, especially with regard
to the food and all possible economies. - So far we have both still been
rather tired and I was at home with a disagreeable cold for some days.
So we declined all invitations for receptions, cocktails etc. and just saw
privately a few friends. We have Portuguese lessons every day and can speak
although with many mistakes, almost all that is necessary and even
carry on a conversation in Portuguese if there is no other way out. But it
is rather an ugly language and a great pity that just this country does not
belong to the Spanish group. Spanish is so much easier for us and so much
more beautiful as language. - The above address remains valid even when
we are in Petropolis.
Love and kisses
Lotte.
pages.notes: Brief von Lotte Zweig an ihre Mutter. Handschrift in violetter Tinte auf Briefpapier der 'Editora Guanabara'. Sehr gut lesbar.
Farbskala und Grauskala für Archivierungszwecke über das Dokument gelegt.
